messages:
maria (sec-eng): 🚨 Heads-up — I just noticed an odd outbound request pattern from the oauth-proxy logs that looks like a referer-based SSRF probe. Example: `GET /auth/callback?next=https://internal.service/?q=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data`

jordan (web-front): can you paste the raw log line? which proxy pod?

maria (sec-eng): sure — pod oauth-proxy-7f4c in prod-us-east-1. Log: `2026-03-19T22:14:02Z GET /auth/callback 200 - referer:"https://attacker.example/?r=http://169.254.169.254" user_agent:"curl/7.85"`

ryan (prod-ops): that referer looks crafted. Do we have any open redirects on the auth callback that accept arbitrary next/referrer?

jordan (web-front): oauth-proxy accepts a `next` param that we validate against allowlist, but older clients sometimes used `referer` passthrough for legacy flows. I'll grep for code paths.

lee (sre): quarantine idea: can we block outbound to 169.254.169.254 from the oauth-proxy namespace while we triage? egress rule tweak should be quick.

maria (sec-eng): yes please, egress block is good containment. Also rotate any tokens that might have been exposed via metadata pull.

sec-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-197 — label: potential-ssrf, severity: medium. Assigned to: maria, jordan.

jordan (web-front): quick grep shows `auth/callback` handler does `redirect_to = params[:next] || request.referer` and we only validate `next` but not referer. That explains it.

maria (sec-eng): ok exploit vector: attacker forces user to click a link with crafted referer so server-side makes a backend request using referer value — we need to stop using referer as an input.

ryan (prod-ops): rolling an egress deny for metadata address now on oauth-proxy namespace (will impact any legitimate IMDS calls from that namespace). ETA 2m.

lee (sre): deployed egress rule; network ACL applied. Monitoring for failed legitimate flows.

jordan (web-front): I can push a quick patch to stop reading `request.referer` and default only to validated `next`. Patch: one-liner in oauth handler. I'll open PR and do canary on staging.

maria (sec-eng): add logging for any unexpected referer usage so we can find other endpoints. Also add an alert on outbound requests to 169.254.169.254.

jordan (web-front): PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/web/-/merge_requests/4421 — changes: remove referer fallback, add explicit allowlist check, unit tests.

sec-bot: Deploy started for merge_request 4421 to staging by jordan.

ryan (prod-ops): Found two more odd referer hits from last 24h across oauth-proxy replicas — increasing based on WAF logs. Blocking attacker IP ranges at WAF now.

maria (sec-eng): good. next actions: (1) keep egress block until we've audited all oauth-proxy instances, (2) merge patch and promote after smoke, (3) run access token rotation for any service accounts used by oauth-proxy, (4) update runbook with referer-not-trusted guidance. I'll draft the post-incident note.

lee (sre): monitoring: no errors from staging after patch; canary passed.

jordan (web-front): landed and promoted to prod with zero downtime.

sec-bot: Deploy finished: merge_request 4421 deployed to production by jordan.

maria (sec-eng): confirm egress rule still in place?

ryan (prod-ops): holding egress block for 24h then review logs.

maria (sec-eng): thanks team. I filed follow-ups: DR-120 (audit logs for referer usage), DR-121 (update oauth docs), DR-122 (rotate oauth-proxy service account keys). I'll update #INC-2026-197 with timeline and mitigations. :thumbsup:

jordan (web-front): FYI: small code note added to PR that devs should not rely on `request.referer`. Added a linter rule suggestion.

lee (sre): postmortem reminder: collect timeline and any exposed tokens we rotated.

maria (sec-eng): closing the immediate incident after containment and patch. Will run a sweep for other endpoints that still read referer. If anyone sees odd 169.254 logs from other services ping me.

ryan (prod-ops): thanks, reopening if we see new hits.

maria (sec-eng): archived evidence in the incident ticket and linked logs. Good job everyone.
